place.en: the Assyrian Empire and its neighbours
place.pt: the Assyrian Empire and its neighbours

notYet: Not yet part of the Assyrian Empire and its neighbours

stages.name: Beyond Assyrian rule
stages.desc: Independent kingdoms and tribes outside the empire's grip

stages.name: Assyrian provinces
stages.desc: Ruled by Assyrian governors or a king installed by Nineveh

stages.name: Phoenician & western vassals
stages.desc: Tribute-paying kings of the coast and the Levant

stages.name: Rebel Babylonia
stages.desc: Chaldean and Babylonian rebels defying Assyria

stages.name: Elam
stages.desc: The kingdom of Elam, Assyria's rival and the rebels' refuge

stages.name: Devastated or contested
stages.desc: Battlefields, sieges, raids and open revolt

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: The kings of Cyprus, among them Phoenician Kition, acknowledged Sargon II
Lule of Sidon flees to Cyprus, where he dies
Cypriot and Greek-speaking sailors serve in Sennacherib's fleet

states.name: Israel
timeline: Philistine cities and Judah's lowlands are vassals; Samaria and Megiddo are provinces
Ashkelon and Ekron join Hezekiah's revolt; Ekron hands its loyal king Padi to Judah
An Egyptian army is beaten at Eltekeh; Lachish is besieged and sacked
Padi is restored at Ekron; the Philistine cities pay tribute again

states.name: Palestine
timeline: Hezekiah's kingdom of Judah, an Assyrian vassal around Jerusalem
Hezekiah withholds tribute and fortifies Jerusalem
Forty-six Judean towns besieged; Jerusalem blockaded, but not taken
Hezekiah pays a heavy tribute and keeps his throne

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Lule, king of Tyre and Sidon, pays tribute to Assyria
Lule joins the western revolt and withholds tribute
Lule flees to Cyprus; Sennacherib installs Ethbaal at Sidon; Byblos and Arvad submit
Sailors of Tyre and Sidon crew Sennacherib's fleet on the Gulf

states.name: Syria
timeline: The old kingdoms of Damascus, Hamath and Arpad are Assyrian provinces
Sennacherib's army marches south toward the Phoenician coast
Syrian shipwrights, deported to Nineveh, build the king's ships; more are built at Til-Barsip

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Sargon II is killed in battle in Tabal; his body is never recovered
Tabal and the Anatolian plateau slip from Assyrian control
Assyrian generals crush the revolt of Kirua of Illubru in Cilicia
Til-Garimmu on the Anatolian frontier is besieged and destroyed
Anatolia beyond the frontier provinces stays independent

states.name: Iraq
timeline: The Assyrian heartland around Assur and Nineveh; Babylon ruled by the Assyrian king since 710
Marduk-apla-iddina seizes Babylon; Sennacherib defeats him at Cutha and Kish
Bel-ibni, raised at the Assyrian court, rules Babylon for Sennacherib
Sennacherib makes his eldest son, Ashur-nadin-shumi, king of Babylon
The Elamites seize Ashur-nadin-shumi at Sippar and crown Nergal-ushezib in Babylon
Nergal-ushezib is captured near Nippur; Mushezib-Marduk takes Babylon's throne
The Battle of Halule on the Tigris ends in a bloody stalemate
Assyrian armies close in on Babylon; the siege begins
Babylon falls after a long siege and is destroyed; the south is Assyrian again

states.name: Iran
timeline: Elam under Shutruk-Nahhunte II, rival of Assyria and refuge of Babylonian rebels
Sennacherib campaigns in the Zagros against the Kassites and Ellipi, on Elam's borders
Hallushu-Inshushinak overthrows his brother and takes Elam's throne
The Assyrian fleet raids the Elamite coast at Nagitu, Hilmu, Pillatu and Hupapanu
Sennacherib invades Elam; Hallushu is killed by his own people; winter storms halt the Assyrians
Humban-nimena takes Elam's throne and pays Babylon's silver to raise an army
Elam's grand coalition marches to Halule
Humban-nimena, paralysed by a stroke, cannot come to Babylon's aid

states.name: Saudi Arabia
timeline: Arab tribes of the northern desert, beyond Assyrian rule
Assyrian troops pursue the Arab queen Te'elhunu to Adummatu
The desert tribes remain beyond Assyria's reach

states.name: Kuwait
timeline: The Sea-Land marshes at the head of the Gulf, home of the Chaldeans of Bit-Yakin
Sennacherib ravages Bit-Yakin; Marduk-apla-iddina's people flee by boat to Elam
Chaldean refugees and marsh tribes keep defying Assyria from both shores
The Assyrian fleet gathers at Bab-salimeti before crossing to the Elamite shore
The Chaldean Mushezib-Marduk rallies the south against Assyria
With Babylon destroyed, the Sea-Land submits to Assyrian rule

states.name: Jordan
timeline: Ammon, Moab and Edom pay tribute to Assyria
The kings of Ammon, Moab and Edom bring gifts to Sennacherib

states.name: N. Cyprus
timeline: Northern Cyprus: island kings who acknowledged Sargon II
Cyprus shelters the fugitive king Lule

events.title: Sargon II falls
events.text: Sennacherib's father dies in battle in Tabal; his body is lost, a terrible omen for Assyria.

events.title: Sennacherib crowned
events.text: Sennacherib succeeds his father and soon abandons Dur-Sharrukin for Nineveh.

events.title: Dur-Sharrukin abandoned
events.text: Sargon's unfinished capital is left behind, tainted by his unburied death.

events.title: Merodach-baladan returns
events.text: The Chaldean Marduk-apla-iddina seizes Babylon with Elamite help.

events.title: Battle of Kish
events.text: Sennacherib routs the Chaldeans and Elamites near Kish; the rebel king flees to the marshes.

events.title: Bel-ibni enthroned
events.text: A Babylonian raised at the Assyrian court is made king of Babylon.

events.title: Zagros campaign
events.text: Sennacherib campaigns against the Kassites and Ellipi in the mountains east of Babylonia.

events.title: Lule flees
events.text: Lule, king of Tyre and Sidon, flees by ship to Cyprus as the Assyrian army nears.

events.title: Ethbaal at Sidon
events.text: Sennacherib installs Ethbaal on the throne of Sidon and takes tribute from the coast.

events.title: Byblos and Arvad submit
events.text: The kings of Byblos and Arvad bring tribute to the Assyrian camp.

events.title: Battle of Eltekeh
events.text: Sennacherib defeats an Egyptian and Kushite army in the plain of Philistia.

events.title: Siege of Lachish
events.text: Judah's second city is stormed with ramps and rams; its siege later fills a palace hall.

events.title: Jerusalem blockaded
events.text: Hezekiah is shut in 'like a bird in a cage', but the city is not taken.

events.title: Ekron punished
events.text: Ekron's rebel leaders are executed and its loyal king Padi restored.

events.title: Ammon, Moab and Edom
events.text: The kings east of the Jordan send gifts to Sennacherib.

events.title: Bit-Yakin ravaged
events.text: Sennacherib ravages the Chaldean marshes; their people sail to the Elamite shore.

events.title: A son for Babylon
events.text: Ashur-nadin-shumi, Sennacherib's eldest son, becomes king of Babylon.

events.title: Mount Nipur
events.text: Sennacherib leads a mountain campaign against the villages of Mount Nipur.

events.title: Hallushu of Elam
events.text: Hallushu-Inshushinak seizes Elam's throne from his brother.

events.title: Revolt in Cilicia
events.text: Assyrian generals storm Illubru and crush the revolt of Kirua.

events.title: Til-Garimmu destroyed
events.text: An Assyrian army destroys Til-Garimmu on the Anatolian frontier.

events.title: Shipyards of Nineveh
events.text: Syrian shipwrights build tall ships 'in the style of their land' at Nineveh.

events.title: Ships at Til-Barsip
events.text: A second squadron is built on the Euphrates and sails downstream.

events.title: Down the Tigris
events.text: Tyrian, Sidonian and Ionian crews sail the fleet down the Tigris to Opis.

events.title: Dragged overland
events.text: From Opis the ships are hauled over dry land on rollers to a canal of the Euphrates.

events.title: Camp at Bab-salimeti
events.text: A tidal surge floods the army's camp at the sea; soldiers live on the ships for five days.

events.title: Gifts for Ea
events.text: Sennacherib casts a golden boat, fish and crab into the Gulf for the god Ea.

events.title: Raid on Nagitu
events.text: The fleet lands on the Elamite coast and carries off Chaldean refugees.

events.title: Sippar falls
events.text: Elam's king strikes behind the fleet and takes Sippar.

events.title: The king's son seized
events.text: Babylonians hand Ashur-nadin-shumi to the Elamites; he vanishes into Elam.

events.title: Battle near Nippur
events.text: Nergal-ushezib, Elam's king in Babylon, is captured and taken to Nineveh.

events.title: Invasion of Elam
events.text: Sennacherib burns Elamite towns until cold and rain halt his army.

events.title: Mushezib-Marduk
events.text: A Chaldean chief takes Babylon's throne and keeps the war going.

events.title: Esagila's treasure
events.text: Babylon pays Elam with silver and gold from Marduk's temple.

events.title: Battle of Halule
events.text: Assyria meets Elam's grand coalition on the Tigris; both sides claim it.

events.title: Arab campaign
events.text: Assyrians take Adummatu, the desert refuge of the Arab queen Te'elhunu.

events.title: Siege of Babylon
events.text: Assyrian armies encircle Babylon; famine grips the city.

events.title: Elam's king stricken
events.text: Humban-nimena suffers a stroke and Elam cannot help its ally.

events.title: Babylon destroyed
events.text: The city falls; its temples are wrecked and canal water is turned through the ruins.

events.title: Marduk carried off
events.text: The statue of Babylon's god is taken to Assyria.

chartNote: Share of the mapped area, by the political situation of each present-day country (Turkey and Saudi Arabia only within the map's frame). Regions are today's boundaries, not ancient ones; each is shown by its dominant situation in a year, a deliberate simplification. Iraq held both the Assyrian heartland and Babylonia, and Iran is shown as Elam, which ruled only its southwest.
chartTitle: The Near East by Assyrian control
